In 102 patients without cirrhosis (21 HCC and 81 controls), the intention-to-diagnose analyses showed that haptoglobin bifucosylated tetra-antennary glycan alone had a sensitivity of 71% (15/21;95%CI 50-86), significantly better (P=0.02) than standard AFP (43%;9/21;95%CI 24-63), and a specificity of 96% (78/81;95% 90-99).

The sensitivity of LCR-glycan, in patients without cirrhosis, was 86% (18/21; 95%CI 63-95) significantly better (P=0.001) than standard AFP (43%; 9/21; 95%CI 24-63), with an AUROC of 0.943 (95%CI 0.806-0.98) compared to 0.811 (95%CI 0.630-0.908) for AFP (P=0.06).
Haptoglobin bifucosylated tetra-antennary glycan is associated with the presence of HCC in patients with chronic liver disease including those without cirrhosis.

title: Serum Levels and Glycosylation Changes of Alpha-1-Acid Glycoprotein According to Severity of Breast Cancer in Korean Women.

screening.reason: The study reports AGP glycosylation changes (fucosylation, high‑mannose, sialylation) that differ with breast cancer stage, suggesting a biomarker for early detection. However, the abstract lacks quantitative performance metrics (e.g., AUC, sensitivity/specificity), so full text is needed to assess the biomarker details.
